text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index closed slightly lower on Wednesday as the market's record-breaking post-election surge finally ran into the sand.Ending an unpredecented eight-session run of record closing highs, and finishing lower for the first time in the 12 sessions since the May 1 election, the blue chip UK index closed 4.1 points lower at 4,686.9.

FRANKFURT - German shares weakened in bourse trade on Wednesday after shock news that Bonn was considering selling some of its shares in Deutsche Telekom, but the market showed no sign of abandoning its record levels. The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session down 21.46 points, or 0.6 percent, at 3,573.69. In post-bourse trade the index was up 29.28 at 3,588.57.

PARIS - French shares ended 2.02 percent higher on an historic closing high on Wednesday after a strong rally on the back of recent opinion polls which took away uncertainty about the upcoming elections. The CAC-40 closed 55.05 points up at 2,774.63. ZURICH - Swiss shares hit a new record closing high for a third time in a row with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ending above 5,100 points following a one percent jump. Dealers said massive foreign buying, Wall Street strength, the U.S. dollar recovery, and technical buying led to the leap. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 26.81 points to close at 3,239.68.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed modestly higher on Wednesday, but recent bullishness in blue-chip issues was watered down by concerns over Sumitomo Trust & Banking Co Ltd's equity financing. The Nikkei 225 closed up 80.61 points or 0.40 percent at 20,209.72.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index roared to a new all-time high on Wednesday, bursting through 14,000 points and closing above that level for the first time ever as HSBC Holdings led a powerful advance. The blue-chip index jumped 247.12 points, or 1.78 percent, to close at an all-time high of 14,153.58.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market ended just lower on Wednesday after a day of lacklustre trade with little impact from Tuesday's Federal government budget. The All Ordinaries index lost 3.9 points to close at 2,530.4.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial shares finish slightly firmer after retracing earlier losses in active afternoon trade. Dealers say industrials cheered by positive start of Wall Street and some futures play. Industrials last up 19.2 points at 8,493.9, golds down 5.3 points at 1,270.1 and the all-share was up 21.4 points at 7,214.5.
